newsitem.title: TURKEY: Armed group holds up tourists in southern Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Armed group holds up tourists in southern Turkey.

text.p: Unidentified armed assailants on Friday held up a group of Italian and Belgian tourists at a roadblock in southern Turkey and set fire to their vehicles , Anatolian news agency reported.
"Seven or eight armed people ordered the tourists out of their vehicles. After that they turned the jeeps over and burned them," Antalya governor Husnu Tuglu was quoted as telling the agency.
He said none of the 40-strong group of tourists was injured or kidnapped in the incident near the popular resort of Kemer, near Antalya, but their shoes were taken so they could not go for help.
Eight of eleven jeeps were burned out and a further two were pushed over a cliff, the agency said.
There were indications that the armed group, which fled into nearby hills, belonged to the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), Tuglu said.
Friday is the thirteenth anniversary of the start of the PKK's armed struggle against the Turkish state for self rule in the southeast of the country.
More than 26,000 people have died in the fighting.
The guerrillas have in the past targeted tourist centres as part of its separatist campaign.
